rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon's military power extended over land and sea; Islahi says its details are mentioned in Sūrah al-Anbiyā’.
rows.anchor: military might both in the land

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David and Solomon did not attribute their kingdom and scientific advances to themselves; they remained grateful for God's blessing.
rows.anchor: never for a moment did they conceitedly think that all this was because of their personal effort

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about being favored over believing servants makes faith the real superiority; actual superiority is God's favor among believers.
rows.anchor: the real superiority is superiority in faith. A person who does not have it, has nothing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon had land and naval forces, a powerful fleet, and special bird-language knowledge that let him use birds for messages, intelligence, and spying, effectively an air force.
rows.anchor: He would use birds to deliver messages, bring information and spying in a very adept way. In this way, he had also developed an air force.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When granted bird-language knowledge, Solomon told his people it was God's blessing, obliging them to be grateful and obedient.
rows.anchor: he informed his nation that they have been blessed with the knowledge of the language of the birds

rows.speaker: Torah
rows.claim: The Torah portrays Solomon as a mean, materialistic king and attributes polytheism and idol worship to him.
rows.anchor: polytheism and idol worship are attributed to him.

rows.speaker: Book of Kings
rows.claim: The Book of Kings says Solomon regarded his splendor as God-given and urged his nation to thank God.
rows.anchor: in the Book of Kings it is mentioned that he continued to regard his splendour and majesty to be God-given

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds have intellect and can converse; human inability to understand them does not disprove this, and Solomon was specially taught their language.
rows.anchor: The verse clearly shows that birds have intellect and can converse and Solomon (sws) was given special knowledge of it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an says all creation glorifies God beyond human understanding and describes beasts and birds as distinct species or communities.
rows.anchor: every object of the universe glorifies the Almighty but human beings do not understand it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals express emotions through distinct sounds and gestures, and variations in sound form language; gestures also convey meaning as silent language.
rows.anchor: their gestures and body language for the expression

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animal trainers and scientific observers can understand animals' voices and gestures; ant intelligence and dogs' spying skills show the potential of animal abilities.
rows.anchor: scientifically observed these animal forms

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Language arises through cadences and variations of sound among beings with comprehension and sentiments, while gestures amount to silent language.
rows.anchor: cadences and variations of sounds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A governing noun is omitted; the sense is that Solomon's entire army was assembled for inspection.
rows.anchor: A governing noun is suppressed in the expression

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wazʿ means stopping, grasping, or holding; in an army context it means training and categorizing, and verse 19 uses the word in the former sense.
rows.anchor: when it is used in relation to any army, it means “to train” and to “to categorize.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse depicts Solomon inspecting and organizing an assembled force of jinn, humans, and birds.
rows.anchor: jinn, human beings and the birds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parade introduces the forces' extraordinary qualities; when these appeared, Solomon humbly asked God to keep him from straying and to remain grateful.
rows.anchor: instead of being overcome with the pride of invincibility, he humbly bent down before his Lord and pleaded that the Lord should take hold of him lest he goes astray

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valley of the ants may be a place specifically named for ants or simply a place where ants live abundantly.
rows.anchor: place that is famous by this name

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During the parade, an ant warned her clan to enter their holes to avoid being trampled by Solomon's army, which would not notice.
rows.anchor: her clan of the lurking danger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ants show military organization: a chief leads, scouts flank and guard, danger alerts the colony, and the group plans protection; migration carries food and young.
rows.anchor: It is clearly evident that the whole army marches under the leadership of a chief. A line of scouts and volunteers flanks both sides of the army.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ants are an independent class of living organisms with human-like traits; some raise animals, cultivate and store crops, and maintain systems of training, differing chiefly in physical form and status.
rows.anchor: they too are an independent species and class of living organisms, as indicated by the Qur’ ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Said” is literal here, though the Qur’an can use it for gestures; ants include speaking and mute kinds, and Solomon could understand their conversation.
rows.anchor: The word “said” is used literally even though it has been used in the Qur’ ān to refer to speak through gestures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon's God-given ability to understand birds also enabled him to comprehend ants.
rows.anchor: Solomon (sws) had the God-given skill to understand the language of the words, he could also comprehend the conversation of ants.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍāḥikan means joy and happiness; qualifying “smiled” this way rules out a derisive smile.
rows.anchor: Thus he happily smiled at her words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here wazʿ means to grasp and stabilize; Solomon asks God to prevent him straying through pride, fulfill duties for favors to himself and his parents, do pleasing deeds, and join the righteous in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: to prevent him from going astray

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode contrasts heedless worldly pride, which turns God's gifts to Satanic aims, with Solomon's recognition of divine help and care not to displease God.
rows.anchor: continued to be mindful of the fact

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the parade inspection, Solomon expressed severe anger when he could not find the lapwing.
rows.anchor: he uttered the above cited words in severe anger.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before “or is he among those absent,” an unstated alternative asks whether the lapwing is present but unseen.
rows.anchor: is it that he is present and I can’t see him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon's trained birds gathered intelligence, delivered messages, and spied; understanding their language enabled him to use them better than modern scientists.
rows.anchor: Since he understood the language of the birds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah omits Solomon's use of birds, but tells how Noah sent a dove to estimate floodwaters; its return with a fresh olive branch showed the water had receded.
rows.anchor: when Noah (sws) wanted to estimate the level of water after the deluge, he sent forth a dove. She came back with a fresh branch of olive in her beak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah inferred that floodwaters had receded after the dove returned with a fresh olive branch; Islahi uses the episode to say bird training dates from the beginning of history.
rows.anchor: from the beginning of history

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doves deliver messages and assess conditions; lapwings were abundant in Palestine and skilled for such tasks, so Solomon used one and demanded strict military discipline.
rows.anchor: were required to follow a strict military discipline

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Islahi's view, Solomon is the subject of the verb makatha; the lapwing soon arrived and gave its report.
rows.anchor: The subject of the verb ﻣَﻜَﺚَ is Solomon (sws) in my opinion. Soon, the lapwing arrived and presented him with the report

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land of Saba lay in southwest Arabia, in the regions of Hadramawt and Asir.
rows.anchor: The territory of Sab ā lies in the south west of Arabia where Ḥadrmawt and ‘As īr are located.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lapwing did not mean Solomon knew nothing about nearby Saba: the queen knew of him, and his fleet traveled far; the bird offered fresh, detailed information to supplement his knowledge.
rows.anchor: What the lapwing actually meant was that he had ret urned with a fresh detailed report that will add to Solomon’s information.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lapwing's words excuse its absence by presenting certain, up-to-date news, as envoys and informants do for rulers.
rows.anchor: news that was certain and also the latest

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lapwing reports in wonder that a woman rules Saba and possesses a very great throne.
rows.anchor: a woman was ruling the land of Sab ā and the style of the report reflects wonder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the inference that Solomon was wholly ignorant of nearby Saba: its queen knew of his wisdom, and his naval fleet traveled to distant lands.
rows.anchor: How can he be totally unaware of such a close by country

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen's people worship the sun and other immoral practices; Satan made these acts seem fair until worship of the one God was lost.
rows.anchor: made to seem fair to them by Satan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen's throne reflected royal splendor; rulers' crowns and thrones were adorned with gold, silver, and other expensive metals.
rows.anchor: gold, silver and other expensive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi holds that these two verses are God's insertion, not part of the lapwing's speech, linking the discourse to Arabia at the Qur'an's revelation.
rows.anchor: By adding these words, the discourse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The insertion says Satan diverted them from the God who reveals hidden things in heaven and earth, knows what is concealed and revealed, and owns the glorious throne.
rows.anchor: what people conceal and what they reveal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because “knows what you conceal and what you reveal” is unsuitable for a lapwing to say, Islahi takes these words as God's own speech.
rows.anchor: Only God can utter them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word al-khabʾ refers to what is hidden and revealed by God in heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: all the hidden things of the heavens and the earth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden things of heaven include the sun, moon, rain, plants, Venus, and Mercury; those of earth include vegetation, trees, seas, and springs, all created and governed by God.
rows.anchor: the sun, the moon, the rain

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord of the great cosmic throne means people must worship Him alone; no earthly throne compares with His.
rows.anchor: No throne however grand it may be
